international.title: Burnham should ‘move on’ from Brexit, says Theresa May, as critics hit out over closer EU ties – UK politics live
international.summary: Issue dominates Sunday broadcast round following Friday’s deals on trade and youth mobility Theresa May ‘aghast’ at Andy Burnham’s talk about rejoining EU Tory deputy head Alex Burghart has been arguing against the deals on Sky and the BBC this morning. He argues the removal of red tape on food and agricultural products is “really bad for business” as British farmers now will have to follow EU regulations when some don’t even trade with the bloc. He says this is a “a huge deadweight cost for them”, and that that the EU has added even more regulations in recent years. What I saw was that the extent of those negotiations, the hours that have to be put in - it’s across the whole of government. It’s not just prime ministerial time, cabinet ministers’ time, officials’ time, to-ing and fro-ing on those negotiations. Because you have to negotiate hard in order to make sure that you’re getting out what you want. And that’s one of the reasons why I look slightly aghast at what Andy Burnham is talking about, further negotiations of going into the EU. And also we, as a country, we voted for Brexit. When I was prime minister I was very clear, we should deliver on that vote. Continue reading...
